newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks can't stay above 7,200, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks can't stay above 7,200, end lower.

text.p: Taiwan shares failed to hold onto gains that pushed the index above six-year resistance at 7,200 points, turning lower at Friday's close despite a strong open.
The index ended down 33.00 points or 0.46 percent at 7,173.42, well back from a midsession high of 7,256.79.
Turnover was a relatively active T$74.93 billion.
Brokers attributed the fall to a lack of a momentum leader.

"Most of the bellwether shares in the recent rally faced downward corrections. Some investors tried to buy speculative shares to support the market, but this failed," said National Securities international sales chief Oliver Fang.

Shares in the plastics sector fell most, with China Petrochemical down T$1 to T$37.9. Formosa Plastics group shares, which had led the index its its rise above 7,200 on Thursday, were among those to fall, with Formosa Plastics down T$1 to T$68.5 and Formosa Chemical Fiber down 70 cents to T$43.2.
Financials and electronics, two other market-leading sectors in the recent rally, also turned weak.

Defying the trend on speculative buying were asset-backed firms, those with abundant real estate assets. Ta Jung Transport gained T$1.7 to T$51.5. Construction shares rose on a property market recovery, with Pao Shiang up T$1.7 to T$26.4.
Brokers said sentiment was cooled somewhat by reduced margin buying after the index closed above 7,200 on Thursday.
The index's drive above 7,200 points triggered exchange rules mandating reduced margin buying to cool speculation.
The margin-buying ratio -- the degree to which securities finance firms can lend to investors -- was cut to 50 percent of a share's purchase price from 60 percent under the rule shift.
"Reduced margin buying will limit some buying power but many investors feel the effect should be short term," Fang said.
For Saturday, consolidation around 7,100-7,200 was seen.
